fullPassage: The English language has words for hundreds of emotions. Other languages have far fewer; for example, there are just seven in the Chewong language of the Malay Peninsula. As one emotion researcher put it, "Different languages recognize different emotions. They carve up the domain of emotion differently." That's not to say that different people experience different emotions, but rather that the categories of emotion identified in various cultures are somewhat arbitrary. That supports the idea that our feelings are not, as Darwin believed, innate hardwired responses to a set of archetypal stimuli. In an article co-authored with Ralph Adolphs, Barrett argued that science has not yet identified truly objective criteria to reliably determine whether a person or an animal is in one emotional state or another. Adolphs, like the majority of emotion researchers, recognizes her point, but wouldn't go that far in dismissing the usual categories. As to which school of thought is correct, the jury is still out.

questions.stem: 다음 밑줄 친 (A)와 (B)의 state의 문맥적 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) state = (감정) 상태, 상황 / (B) state = (행정 구역) 주
det.analysis:
✅ ① (감정) 상태 — (행정 구역) 주: (A)는 emotional state로 '감정 상태', (B)는 largest state로 '주(행정 구역)' ←정답
❌ ② (행정 구역) 주 — (감정) 상태: (A)와 (B)의 의미가 뒤바뀜
❌ ③ (감정) 상태 — 진술하다: (B)의 state는 명사 '주'이지 동사 '진술하다'가 아님
❌ ④ 진술하다 — (행정 구역) 주: (A)의 state는 '상태'이지 '진술하다'가 아님
det.tip: state: 상태(명사) / 주(행정 구역, 명사) / 진술하다(동사) — 문맥으로 구별

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "things in the environment that cause a reaction or response in a person or an animal"

det.korean: 반응을 일으키는 것들 → stimuli(자극)
det.analysis:
❌ ① languages(언어) — 반응을 일으키는 자극이 아님
✅ ② stimuli(자극) — 사람이나 동물에게 반응을 일으키는 것들 ←정답
❌ ③ emotions(감정) — 자극에 대한 반응 자체이지 자극이 아님
❌ ④ cultures(문화) — 정의와 무관
det.tip: stimuli = 자극 (반응을 일으키는 것). archetypal stimuli = 전형적 자극

questions.passage: That supports the idea that our feelings are not, as Darwin believed, innate hardwired responses to a set of archetypal stimuli. In an article co-authored with Ralph Adolphs, Barrett argued that science has not yet __________ (identify) truly objective criteria to reliably determine whether a person or an animal is in one emotional state or another.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.korean: has not yet + 과거분사(현재완료). identify → identified
det.analysis: 'science has not yet __________'에서 앞에 has가 있으므로 현재완료(have/has + 과거분사)예요. 그래서 identify를 과거분사 identified로 바꿔요. '아직 ~하지 못했다'는 뜻이에요.
det.tip: has not yet + 과거분사: has not yet identified (현재완료)

questions.passage: In an article co-authored with Ralph Adolphs, Barrett argued that science has not yet identified truly objective criteria to __________ (reliable) determine whether a person or an animal is in one emotional state or another. Adolphs, like the majority of emotion researchers, recognizes her point, but wouldn't go that far in dismissing the usual categories.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.korean: 동사 determine을 꾸미는 자리이므로 형용사 reliable을 부사 reliably로 바꾼다
det.analysis: 빈칸 뒤 determine(판단하다)은 동사예요. 동사를 꾸미는 것은 부사이므로 형용사 reliable(신뢰할 수 있는)을 부사 reliably(신뢰성 있게)로 바꿔요. '신뢰성 있게 판단하다'라는 뜻이 돼요.
det.tip: reliable(형용사) → reliably(부사): 동사 determine을 수식

questions.passage: The English language has words for hundreds of emotions. Other languages have far fewer; for example, there are just seven in the Chewong language of the Malay Peninsula. As one emotion researcher put it, "Different languages recognize different emotions. They carve up the domain of emotion differently." That's not to say that different people experience different emotions, but rather that the categories of emotion identified in various cultures are somewhat arbitrary. That supports the idea that our feelings are not, as Darwin believed, innate hardwired responses to a set of archetypal stimuli. In an article co-authored with Ralph Adolphs, Barrett argued that science has not yet identified truly objective criteria to reliably determine whether a person or an animal is in one emotional state or another. Adolphs, like the majority of emotion researchers, recognizes her point, but wouldn't go that far in dismissing the usual categories. As to which school of thought is correct, __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 어느 학파가 옳은지에 대해서는 아직 '결론이 나지 않았다(the jury is still out)'
det.analysis:
❌ ① the answer is obvious(답이 명백하다) — 두 견해가 대립 중이라 명백하지 않음
❌ ② everyone agrees now(이제 모두 동의한다) — 여전히 논쟁 중이라 반대
✅ ③ the jury is still out(아직 결론이 나지 않았다) — 어느 학파가 옳은지 미결 상태 ←정답
❌ ④ Darwin was clearly right(다윈이 분명히 옳았다) — 본문은 어느 쪽도 결론 내리지 않음
det.tip: the jury is still out = 아직 결론이 나지 않았다(미결)
